newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Ousted Afghan forces shell strategic pass.
newsitem.headline: Ousted Afghan forces shell strategic pass.

text.p: Forces belonging to the ousted Afghan government on Friday shelled and rocketed a strategic pass north of the capital Kabul held by the radical Islamic Taleban militia.

Forces under ousted government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood, along with those of northern Uzbek leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum, are fighting to retake Kabul from the Taleban, who captured the city at the end of last month. The Taleban control of over two-thirds of the country.
"We must keep fighting, we can't let them rest," said Najim Khan, one of Masood's commanders directing rocket fire onto Taleban positions on the De Sabz pass, around 30 km (19 miles) north of Kabul.

"We're shelling to keep them busy so they can't bring up reinforcements," he said, speaking on top of a mud-walled compound and scanning the pass through field glasses near Bagram, 45 km (28 miles) north of Kabul.
Masood's forces launched a major attack on Tuesday to secure the De Sabz pass, which would give the commander a strategically vital position over Kabul, but have so far failed to capture it.
Down the road from Khan's base, three families with donkeys and a camel loaded with carpets and belongings moved across the dusty plain heading east for the village of Nejrab.
The women, wearing long crimson scarves and blue leggings, carried the smaller children.
"We have to leave because of the fighting," said 35-year-old Myagul (one name), a switch in his hand and his three-year-old son strapped to his back with a wool blanket.

Warplanes belonging to the radical Islamic Taleban militia bombed the town of Jabal os-Siraj, 70 km (44 miles) north of the capital where Masood is headquartered, on Friday but there was no word on casualties.

The first plane flew in from behind the Hindu Kush mountains, attracting a burst of anti-aircraft fire, and dropped a bomb into a nearby field throwing up a cloud of dust at around 7.20 a.m. (0250 GMT).
Taleban planes flew two more sorties over the town as the menfolk gathered for Friday prayers just after midday.
At least 14 people died in an air attack on the village of Kalakan, 25 km (15 miles) north of Kabul, on Thursday.
